fields.meta_title: Color Personality Quiz: What Color Are You? | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take an eight-question color personality quiz that names your color, or build one that recommends products and saves each answer.
fields.h1: Build a Color Personality Quiz That Names Your Color
fields.hero_description: Build a color personality quiz that names a color and saves every answer, or take the eight-question quiz below.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Color Personality Quiz Built With Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Describe your colors and what each result should show. Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it, and changes any part when you ask.
fields.feature_1:
Every option points to a color

Name four colors in your prompt, such as Orange, Blue, Green, and Purple, and every answer option is mapped to one of them. The color with the most picks becomes the result, and a tie goes to the color you listed first.
fields.feature_2:
A result page with a next step

The result screen names the color and describes what the answers lean toward. Below it, show what fits that color for your audience: three products from your shop, a paint palette, or a class project to start.
fields.feature_3:
Each finished quiz saved as a row

Every play lands in a database you own, with each pick, the color it scored, and the time it finished. Filter the table by color before a sale or a workshop and see exactly who landed where.
fields.feature_4:
A live count of colors in the room

Put a live chart on a second screen and watch it count each color as people finish. A facilitator can project it while a group takes the quiz on their phones and start the talk from the real split.
fields.feature_5:
One question per phone screen

Players tap through one question per screen with a progress bar, which suits a link shared in a text or a QR code on a counter. Emergent puts no cap on how many responses the quiz collects.
fields.feature_6:
Results sent where you already work

The app can post each finished result to Slack or send you an email with the color. It can also pass the player's email to your email tool through its API, onto a list for that color.

plan.angle: The top 10 is consumer color tests and kids' quizzes that name a color and stop there. A visitor plays a full eight-question color personality quiz on this page, then sees four builds that do something with the color: a candle shop that recommends three candles per result and segments its list, an interior design studio that turns a result into a paint palette and a consult request, an offsite facilitator who projects a live tally of colors in the room, and a seventh-grade art teacher who opens a painting project per color with no names saved. The FAQ covers picking the colors, mapping answers so every result can win, fair wording, and what the result page should show.
tab_stories: Hollow Pine Candle Co. runs the color personality quiz on its shop, Tessa Morgan lands on Ocean Blue, the result page shows the 3 candles the owner picked for blue, and her email joins the Ocean Blue list in the shop's email tool through its API.

Calloway Interiors puts the quiz on its homepage, Marcus Webb lands on Forest Green and sees a 4-swatch paint palette, he requests a consult, and designer Ines Calloway gets a Slack message with his result and palette.
Dana Kowalski opens a two-day offsite with the quiz, 24 people take it on their phones, and the projector shows a live count of Orange 9, Blue 7, Green 5, and Purple 3 as answers land.
Mr. Okafor gives the quiz to his seventh-grade art class with no names saved, each result opens a painting project in that color family, and 27 students start their projects the same period.
